stemMarkdown: Find the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs. 23000 at 20% per annum for 2 years. (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: CI: the amount after 2 years is $33120.00$, so CI $= 10120.00$. SI $= \dfrac{23000 \times 20 \times 2}{100} = 9200.00$. The difference is $920.0$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For 2 years the gap is always the interest earned on the first year's interest: $P\left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2 = 23000 \times \left(\dfrac{20}{100}\right)^2 = 920.0$.
